title: The Lankavatara Sutra — the Sanskrit text
textType: Mahayana sutra in prose and verse
attributionNote: A Mahayana sutra transmitted without an author, studied above all in the Yogācāra schools: the Buddha is asked at Laṅkā by the lord of the yakṣas for the teaching he keeps at heart. GRETIL's e-text follows P. L. Vaidya's edition (Darbhanga 1963, Buddhist Sanskrit Texts 3) and was input by the Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon Input Project.
description: The Laṅkāvatāra is the sutra of the mind and of what it constructs: that the world of objects is nothing but the storehouse consciousness and the discriminating mind, that the tathāgatagarbha is present in every being, that the doctrines of the śrāvakas, the other philosophical schools and the mistaken teachers are answered by the teaching of no-self and of the emptiness of what is dependently arisen, and, in its chapter on meat eating, that the Bodhisattva out of compassion eats no flesh. Its verses on the pure mind, the stages of the Bodhisattva and the entrance into the wisdom of the Buddha run through the traditions of Chan, Zen and the Tibetans.
historicalContext: Compiled over several centuries and translated into Chinese and Tibetan, the sutra became the scripture of Bodhidharma's line and the object of a long commentarial tradition in East Asia; the Sanskrit text survives in the Nepalese manuscripts Vaidya edited.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: all nine chapters with their prose and verse, 1,313 passages, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. The file prints its own title and the first chapter's heading above the text, and the reader drops them. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
